failure_reason: POLICY BLOCK, not a technical block: amazon.ae's robots.txt (https://www.amazon.ae/robots.txt, verified live via Claude-in-Chrome navigation/get_page_text this session, HTTP 200 rendered content) contains explicit, separate 'Disallow: /' directives naming Claude/Anthropic crawlers by name: 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' (appears twice), 'User-agent: Claude-User', 'User-agent: Claude-SearchBot', and 'User-agent: Claude-Web' -- each its own group with a full-site 'Disallow: /'. This is distinct from and far more restrictive than the generic 'User-agent: *' group at the top of the file, which only disallows a specific list of account/cart/review/wishlist/sign-in utility paths and otherwise permits crawling. Per the brief's mandatory §5 instruction ('Check robots.txt for a Claude-specific Disallow: / before extracting... means STOP and mark the company blocked with that finding') and this project's established precedent of treating a targeted, named Claude-specific full-site disallow as a deliberate publisher opt-out to respect -- not a generic anti-bot wall to route around -- extraction was stopped before any category tree, mega-menu, or qty work was attempted. This matches the identical finding from the prior Home-Decor pass on this same company (archive c189, same robots.txt lines), independently re-verified here via the Chrome connector rather than taking the prior pass's HTTP-layer finding on faith. No WAF-bypass or alternate-route technique was attempted, per policy.
notes: Prior Home-Decor pass (notes/285.md, archive c189) found the identical robots.txt Claude-disallow and stopped before extraction, also noting the site is live (its homepage returned an AWS WAF JS-challenge interstitial to a non-Claude UA, confirming the site is up and merely bot-protected, not retired). This session independently re-verified the robots.txt finding using the mandated Claude-in-Chrome browser connector (own isolated tab, tabId 1961720133, created via tabs_create_mcp, closed via tabs_close_mcp on completion; no other worker's tab was touched): navigated to https://www.amazon.ae/robots.txt and read the full rendered text with get_page_text. The file lists (in addition to the generic '*' group) explicit disallow-all groups for many named AI/LLM crawlers -- GPTBot, CCBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, ClaudeBot (x2), Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-Web, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, DeepSeekBot, xAI-Grok, and dozens more -- confirming this is a deliberate, comprehensive AI-crawler opt-out policy, not an oversight or a generic anti-scrape measure aimed at something else. No category tree, mega-menu, sitemap, or product/qty data was accessed or extracted; only the robots.txt file itself was read, per the brief's explicit sanction to check robots.txt before extracting. Flagging for the orchestrator/other workers: this reconfirms Amazon UAE (SR 285) as blocked for the Furniture pass on the same grounds as the Home-Decor pass; Noon UAE (SR 191, also flagged as a marketplace needing the same check) should get an equivalent robots.txt verification if not already done, per the prior pass's note.
